title: Session sync after the twenty-sixth notes and THE ENDING: lessons, and the owner's twenty-seventh notes queued for the next session
context: Nine commits since the last sync (7bc7ef58..78b55764): the back gate's shoulders, the welcome's keywords sound, the view back after the study, SOL's first aim, and THE ENDING in five steps (2026-10-06-the-ending-plan-and-the-run-recap). The owner played the build and closes the session ('sync, commit and push, then we will /clear'), handing over the next round's notes.
outcome: Lessons from the round: (1) The view-back fix passed its own step (--study-view, entered with ?skip=expedition) and still failed in the owner's play: a step that enters a beat through a skip can miss the path the real run takes to it; reproduce from the real handover (the bare page or ?skip at an earlier chapter) before calling a camera fix done. (2) Short all-caps words in a seiyu_voice line are read as letters ('WE DID IT' said I-T): write a shouted line's short words in lower case. (3) --debrief had been red on main since the 2026-10-03 summary page and nobody saw it: a suite that is not in a round's chain can rot; the full default suite (46 steps) is the net. (4) Headless Chrome barely advances the game clock (a SOL pass clock moved 0.47 s in 20 s): motion has to be judged in a real browser or by a pure test. (5) On --dist a bare import of a src module in a step is a second, silent copy; import the page's own ?v= URL. QUEUED, the owner's twenty-seventh notes (2026-10-06), verbatim in substance: 1) sometimes clearing the first landing spot nearby does not unlock the cargo; a hidden unregistered enemy is suspected: it shows on the radar but not on the screen. 2) Still not solved: after the 'language analysis' the player is set to a bird's-eye view; go back to whichever view was interrupted. 3) The second-closest cargo/rocket: there is STILL a problem going through narrow tiles with the MÖRK. 4) The squads (multiple units managed together to spare the frame rate): their clusters should be a) closer together and b) slightly staggered; otherwise how they move looks unnatural and unorganic. 5) With it: not for the earlier waves, which are not that big; use the trick only when there are hundreds or thousands of units, and mix regular single bodies with the mixed 5x ones; goal, a compromise between frame rate and looking organic. 6) When Isao builds it should look like he is dropping filament; there used to be an effect, it is no longer seen. 7) Tactical nuke: '1 per wave' is set, but sometimes when the player takes over there is no nuke available; increase the nukes: even if the auto gunship shot one, a player who takes over can shoot one too (shooting too many and closing a tremor hole early already costs biomass). 8) Walls from breaches not fully rebuilt: better, but edge cases still fail (two owner screenshots, not in the repo: one breach successfully covered by a run of kit walls, one failure with a few lone segments in an open area). 9) The Dyson preparation: it should show our actual planet, not the placeholder one, and play as a celebration cinematic AFTER the final wave, before the score is looked at. 10) The 'WE DID IT!' line says 'it' as the letters I and T; re-record it as 'WE DID it!'.
evidence: the owner's message of 2026-10-06 (the twenty-seventh notes, two screenshots)
